name: The Sticky Note Myth
why_it_works: Everyone carries a belief they have never checked. Showing that belief on a sticky note feels familiar, and holding the correction until the last slides makes the reader keep swiping to find out if they were wrong, which is the moment they start to trust the expert.

hook.pattern: A handwritten sticky note with a common belief, and the question 'True or false? Answer on the last slide.'
examples: "{{myth}}" True or false? Answer on slide six.
We hear this every week. Most people believe it.
Before you decide anything, check this sticky note.

variables.name: myth
variables.description: The common belief, in the client's words
variables.example: If I'm hurt at work, I can't see my own doctor

variables.name: truth
variables.example: In many states you can choose your own doctor after the first visit; the rules depend on your state

variables.name: reason_one
variables.example: the first clinic you're sent to feels like your only option

variables.name: reason_two
variables.description: What it can cost to believe it
variables.example: people skip care or wait too long to ask

variables.name: next_step
variables.example: a free 15-minute call to check the rules where you live

slides.headline: True or false?
slides.body: "{{myth}}" The answer is on slide six.
slides.visual_prompt: Yellow handwritten sticky note reading the myth, stuck on a wooden desk next to a coffee mug, soft window light, 4:5

slides.headline: Most people say true
slides.body: We hear this from new clients every week.
slides.visual_prompt: Several sticky notes with the same myth on a corkboard, shallow depth of field

slides.headline: Why it sounds right
slides.visual_prompt: Sticky note on a desk next to a stack of paperwork, warm desk lamp

slides.headline: What it can cost you
slides.visual_prompt: Close-up of a calendar with days crossed off, cool light

slides.headline: Ready for the answer?
slides.visual_prompt: Hand reaching to peel the sticky note off the desk, motion blur

slides.headline: The answer
slides.visual_prompt: Sticky note crumpled beside a clean notepad with the correct answer written neatly, bright daylight

slides.headline: Not sure about yours?
slides.visual_prompt: {{firm_name}} logo card in calm brand colors with the next step in large type

cta: Book {{next_step}} with {{firm_name}}; this post is general information, not advice for your situation.

craft.notes: State the myth in the client's own words, give it fair reasons, then correct it gently in one plain sentence. The tone is 'easy mistake', never 'you're dumb'; that respect is what earns the call.

do_not: Pick a myth whose real answer is 'it depends' without saying so
Shame the reader for believing it
Turn the answer into a promise of a result
compliance: Law firm: no guarantees or predictions of case outcomes; label as attorney advertising where your state bar requires; include 'This is general information, not legal advice'
Financial advisor: no promises of returns or income; include required firm disclosures and 'not individual investment advice'
Insurance: do not state coverage as universal; say policies and state rules vary; include license number
Mortgage: no rate or approval promises; include NMLS number and equal housing language
Dental: no claims of painless or guaranteed results; keep clinical statements accurate and general
